newsitem.title: UK: Dioxin found in women 20 years after exposure.
newsitem.headline: Dioxin found in women 20 years after exposure.

text.p: Italian and U.S. researchers said on Friday they had found traces of the toxic chemical dioxin in the bodies of women 20 years after they were exposed in an industrial accident.
Checks on 62 people exposed to dioxin after a 1976 accident near Seveso in Italy showed raised levels in local inhabitants, but especially in women.

Writing in a letter to the Lancet medical journal, the researchers at the University of Milan and the U.S. Centres for Disease Control said they were not sure why this was, but it had implications for the health of both the women and their children.
Dioxins are linked to birth and reproductive defects.
"We gave the participants a questionnaire surveying demographic, lifestyle and accident-related factors, and medical history," they wrote.

"Presence in the contaminated area at the time of the accident, number of years spent in the zone, occupation, and distance from the accident site within the zone did not explain the gender difference," they wrote.
Toxins can accumulate in body fat and women tend to have more body fat than men, but again the researchers were hard-pressed to find an explanation.
"(Dioxin) concentrations were unrelated to percentage body fat, body mass index, height, weight or reported weight loss for each sex," they wrote.

"Increased dioxin concentrations in women may be due to variation in metabolism or elimination, or to differences in body fat or hormone-related factors," they said. But women -- especially of child-bearing age -- should be aware of the findings.
